children: New Era Energy & Digital's revenue fell 7.4% year over year, while its net loss widened as general and administrative expenses rose 346.1%, primarily due to higher stock-based compensation and employee costs from increased headcount. Higher interest income and a gain on the fair value of a derivative liability partly offset the increased operating costs.
¹ Reported as “Total revenues, net”. ² Reported as “Net loss”. ³ Reported as “Net loss per share - basic and diluted”.
: Net revenue rose $13,254, primarily on a $0.20 per Mcf increase in gas prices net of processing and transportation, partly offset by 58 MMcf lower sales volumes.
: Revenue fell $24,991, mainly due to a 507-barrel decrease in sales volumes, partly offset by a $4.77 per barrel price increase.
: In September, the company signed a 20-year agreement for 200 to 207 megawatts of firm electric energy for its Texas data center project.
: The 493-acre TCDC campus is designed for over 1 GW of potential compute capacity, with projected power delivery beginning as early as the end of 2027.
